label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, C, B, B where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Upright cylinder with a top and a bottom chime rim, as the brief's 55-gallon drum needs. All six views (front, left, back, right, top, below) and the four angles show the same outline, with nothing sticking out or missing. The top and bottom rims are faceted, but they stay within the drum's outline.

M2.reason: Measured 23.8 x 23.8 x 36 units against the brief's 23 across and 34 high: 3.5% off across and 5.9% off high, inside the 15% band (measured sizeOff 0.059).

M3.reason: The parts the brief names are present: the drum body, the hazard stripe, and the rust-coloured body. The parts every Valve drum in the line-up shows are also there: the top rim and the bottom rim (chimes). Nothing the brief names or the line-up shows is missing. The top and bottom rims are faceted at about 12 sides; no Valve drum count is given to check that against, so this is not charged.

M4.reason: Brown, rust-stained painted steel on the body, and a greyer, worn metal on the rims, which reads as rusted steel. The yellow and black hazard stripe is painted, as a hazard stripe is. Nothing in the views reads as a wrong colour or material.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe runs at the same height on all four sides, with diagonal yellow and black bands at a similar sharpness. Rust mottling and wear are on the body, and the vertical seam is faint. Nothing is missing from what the brief asks.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the line-up at the game's size, beside three of Half-Life's own, the asset (B in lineup.png) read as one of the game's own. The judges picked other models as the one not made by Valve, and the asset passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The brief names no front, and the drum stands upright on its base as a drum does. The bottom view shows a closed flat base, and the top view a closed lid, so it sits on its origin as a drum should.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors. 264 triangles is under the most Half-Life spends on a prop of its size (422), so it passes the fail band. It is past the third-quartile warning (156), but that is a warning and not a fail. The top and bottom faces are closed in every view, with nothing open, inside out, or floating.
